documents.title: Artificial Intelligence at USD: Guidance and Principles
documents.summary: Central USD page on responsible GenAI use. It gives principles (human judgment, disclosure, verification, privacy, accessibility), names Microsoft Copilot as the approved tool, and leaves AI-use decisions to disciplines and courses.
documents.stance_why: The hub states principles but "should not be viewed as official policy; it is intended to provide guidance", and says "Faculty should make this determination in collaboration with peers" and that AI's "role will vary across disciplines, courses, assignments", so it sets no stance and hands the decision to faculty and courses.

units.why: Opening purpose statement: the page exists "to guide students, faculty, and staff in the ethical and innovative use of generative AI", an institution-level framework covering all audiences.
units.anchor: guide students, faculty, and staff in the ethical and innovative use of generative AI

units.why: Defines GenAI as "a type of artificial intelligence that uses large datasets to generate content", setting what the guidance covers; a definition so P61.
units.anchor: GenAI is a type of artificial intelligence that uses large datasets to generate content
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A (coded P61, actor all, phase general, modality informs, stance neutral). Checked against the source, which says "GenAI is a type of artificial intelligence that uses large datasets to generate content"; it is a real policy statement, so it is kept.

units.why: FAQ definition lists "text, images, code, audio or video" and named tools ("ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini"), defining the scope of covered tools, so P61.
units.anchor: tools that can generate content
units.policy: GenAI refers to tools that generate content such as text, images, code, audio or video from prompts or questions, for example ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini.

units.why: States the university must help stakeholders "navigate this reality" of regular GenAI use, a rationale for engaging rather than banning. P82 is nearest (AI use is a fact that cannot be avoided); P87 (benefits) does not fit as no benefit is named.
units.anchor: people regularly use GenAI
units.policy: Students, faculty, staff and graduates live in a world where people regularly use GenAI, and USD must help them navigate it.
units.fit_note: Says AI use is a fact of the world that USD must help people navigate; it does not say use cannot be verified or prevented.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A (coded P82, actor all, phase general, modality informs, stance neutral). Checked against the source, which says "people regularly use GenAI"; it is a real policy statement, so it is kept.

units.why: Says USD values promoting "technology literacy" and preparing the community for "the workplace"; an AI-for-careers rationale, P44.

units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A (coded P44, actor all, phase general, modality informs, stance neutral). Checked against the source, which says "preparing our community to be successful in the 21st century learning environment and workplace"; it is a real policy statement, so it is kept.

units.why: "USD teaches and empowers our students, faculty and staff to understand and, when appropriate, to utilize with care the latest developments in technology, including GenAI" frames teaching AI literacy for the 21st century workplace, so P44.
units.anchor: USD teaches and empowers our students, faculty and staff to understand
units.fit_note: Encouragement is qualified by 'when appropriate' and 'with care' and does not set a default for coursework.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P02, actor all, phase general, modality informs, stance encourage; coder B coded P44, actor all, phase general, modality informs, stance encourage. The source says "USD teaches and empowers our students, faculty and staff to understand". The sentence commits USD to teaching and empowering people to understand and, when appropriate, use GenAI with care. Its point is AI literacy for the workplace the preceding sentences set up, which is P44; P02 (permit or encourage by default) does not fit because 'when appropriate' sets no default for coursework. The final code is P44, with A's note on the qualification kept.

units.why: "GenAI is an interactive set of tools that, when used, should serve as a supplement to human activity, not a replacement." This keeps humans as primary thinkers, so P32.

The source says "should serve as a supplement to human activity, not a replacement". The sentence says AI 'should serve as a supplement to human activity, not a replacement'. It is a framing principle without a specific limit on any use, so the unit stance is neutral; the overreliance units that name a thing to avoid are the ones coded restrict.

units.why: "USD encourages transparency and accuracy" with "final work, decisions and strategies reflecting human judgment" asks for transparency about AI use; nearest P24, as an encouragement rather than a per-submission rule.

units.fit_note: Encourages transparency in general terms without requiring a statement on each submission; also asks that final work reflect human judgment. | Also asks for accuracy and for final work and decisions to reflect human judgment; no disclosure mechanism is given.

The source says "USD encourages transparency and accuracy in the context of GenAI use". The sentence 'USD encourages transparency and accuracy in the context of GenAI use' asks for disclosure as a condition of use. The encouragement is of transparency, not of AI use itself, so the stance is permit (use with conditions), matching the Principle 3 disclosure unit that both coders coded permit.
